fieldMarks: Coat mostly black and white with hoary fur tips
White patch between the eyes and across the muzzle; white nose tip
Black feet (species name caligata, 'booted'); black cap larger than in other marmots
behavior: Loud short alarm calls; upraised tail signals aggression
Spends about 80% of life in burrows
Hibernates October-February in the south and September-April in British Columbia
Eats almost entirely grasses and other herbaceous plants
habitat: Rocky talus slopes and alpine or subalpine meadows; at sea level in Alaska, higher elevations to the south.
range: Alaska to Yukon and Northwest Territories, south to northeastern Washington, central Idaho and western Montana.

lookalikes.name: Yellow-bellied marmot
lookalikes.howToTell: Lacks black feet and white nose patch; frosted tawny coat.
